This gets a recommendation from me, but I really must stress that it probably won't be everyone's cup of tea.  It's slow, tactical, and can be REALLY punishing for new players.  Make no mistake, reaction speed plays almost no part in this game.  Instead, you'll need to plan ahead and stay aware of where everything sits in the 3D space.  Knowing your own ship, your allies' and your opponents' will take some time and until you do the nasty surprises will keep on coming.
But if you're looking for a good space combat multiplayer, this really brings the fantasy to life.  Everything feels heavy and meaningful,  and your crew jabbering in your ear about how badly you're getting pounded really gives you that sense of commanding a big space submarine.  Do take advantage of the in-game tutorial videos, as they cover all the key points that will help you win.
As a closing note, a lot of recent reviews have been slamming the devs for the new implant system, and I have to agree.  It's a system that rewards long term (or big spending) players (like myself) with potentially huge advantages which is only going to make it harder few new players to succeed.  That said, I still don't think it's any substitute for a good team, and you'll find that when your team works together well, the stats mean a lot less.
Solo grandstanding will get you nothing here, regardless of how many stat boosts you have.

Let me start this review by mentioning that I've been with Okami since it's PS2 days. I bought the remaster on PS3, and having it's on PC is more useful to me as I can take it where I go and I can do things in the background while playing.
This will be a long review, so I'll give a TL:DR here.
Is this game worth £15.99 / $20? Yes.
And now, onto the longer review.
I'll admit that I was dubious when starting up this game, solely because of the keyboard/mouse controls. Like, this was a console game and the Wii port looked very uncomfortable to me, so I thought that PC-controls would be equally bad. I was extremely wrong. The mouse works very well (once my sensitivity was lowered) as a camera, and it's more controllable than it ever was. This means that frustrating levels with thin platforms you have to go across are much easier to do.
Of course, you can change your keybindings but for me, the default are very well-done. Nothing's too difficult for my fairly small hands to reach, and everything feels very polished.
The graphics are wonderful, and it runs very smoothly at 30fps; and I will push that this game is meant for 30fps. After all, it's originally a PS2/PS3 (let's ignore the Wii) port, and that generally ran at 30fps. Since the animations are made for it, it runs very well and I would advise Capcom to keep it capped like this no matter what people say, as the game works best in this. Will it be frustrating for people used to higher? Probably not. You can barely tell it's 30fps. It's ideal.
The minimum specs are probably incorrect as my laptop isn't very high-end. I'm running AMD Radeon R5 and it doesn't stutter the slightest. I expect a lot of computers/laptops can handle it, though be careful if you have a complete potato.
Some people may be tempted to skip the cutscenes, even on their first run through. Don't. The story is beautiful and intricate, the artwork is gorgeous, and overall, it's a very good game plot-wise.
The prologue is long but interesting, and there are many more to come that are just...breathtaking.
Naturally, the soundtrack follows in its footsteps; Okami has one of the best (if not THE best) soundtrack of all time. Considering the game's setting, the music is heavy based around traditional Japanese music, and uses various traditional instruments, too. I won't spoil, but the final boss battle has stunning music and if I were going just from that, I'd still say to buy it.
£15.99/$20 is not much considering the content given. Not only are the graphics hugely upscaled from PS3-days (which was a HD Remaster too), but the game offers hundreds of hours of content. From collectibles such as Stray Beads to just exploring the world, Okami has high replayability and New Game+ is superb in this game; once you complete the game for yourself, you'll see.
With so much to do, it's hard to complain about the price! Keep in mind that this is a classic game originally made back in 2006, so it's eleven years old and it's definitely managed to keep up with more recent games. Even back then, it was ahead of its time; and even now, replaying it makes me realise just how gorgeous it is.
A lot of people compare it to the Legend of Zelda franchise, and they're right to do so! But don't go into the game expecting some sort of Zelda clone - it's unique and the dungeons are very interesting, with puzzles that are surprisingly clever. Also, you play a wolf for 100% of the game so that's...that's definitely different.
If you're a first-time player, you'll definitely find the atmosphere amazing. From unsettling dungeons and monsters to truly heartwarming moments, Okami is a highly emotional game that makes me cry from time to time even when I know what's going to happen. It knows the exact music to use, and knows what sort of tone to set for each step of the plotline (and, my god, it is a long plotline that interests me to no end).
The Celestial Brush feature is best used on PC, as your mouse gives you complete control over it. It's extremely well-ported, and I would recommend this to gamers of any level. To hardcore gamers some of the fights may be easy, but there is a difficulty spike that may come your way! Or you can challenge yourself by using only low-end weapons (the rosary challenge is one of my personal favourites). No matter what you do, Okami always has more and knows how to please its fanbase.
Not to mention that once you complete the game you unlock some bonus content which includes the soundtrack and concept art and, I'm not going to lie to you, it's very much worth it.
Amazing artwork, a great soundtrack, a wonderful plot + good controls for a port; what more could you want? It's a wonderful experience and I really would recommend to try it out.

I am making a YouTube series on Tower Unite and its updates so you can have a look at those videos if you want to see my first impressions visually.
Tower Unite is the successor to Garry's Mod: Tower, a hub to addicting and fun minigames.  This game acts as a casual mmorpg that offers a plentiful amout of customisation to your character and your condo (Your own house where you can decorate and fill with the items you can buy in-game).
The way you can purchase these items are with in-game currency which you collect playing the various minigames on offer.
They are also adamament that there will be NO microtansactions and you pay for the standalone game at a very reasonable price.
Before I get into more detail about the game itself I would like to mention for a an early access build the game runs very smooth on my system (not to say that it shouldn't).  The game also has minimum requirements that can meet a very low end system and the people that could run Garry's Mod: Tower can run this.
The minigames are fairly solid but if you are new to Tower Unite or Garry's Mod: Tower then you may not know what to expect from this game.  Minigolf runs much better than GMOD:Tower as the previous version had very strange ball physics and people use to abuse the phsyics to land shots that would unnaturally ping off walls etc etc...
Virus is also an old classic that runs smoother and has the basic game down to a tee without changing much.  Some of the textures are missiing but this isn't a final product.
Ball game is the most polished of the lot so far but can anly hope for more levels and to be even more perfected.
I havent had much experience on the new game mode but honestly the one time I played it I didn't quite understand what was going on.  So maybe some in-game tutorials might be useful if trying to create new game ideas.
Overall the early access version is only worth getting now if you enjoyed Garry's Mod Tower, otherwise hold on to your hard earned cashuntil a later release.  Definately pick this up if you want to see this game bloom into a beautiful gem in your Steam library.

Astebreed is a shoot em up (shmup) from Developers Edelweiss, well known for selling their products at comiket (the largest conventions for doujin products in japan) These guys live, eat and sleep games development.
Astebreed is a brilliant SHMUP that manages to improve the genre with brilliant mechanics and difficulty that keeps on dragging you back for a second attempt
The game manages to fluidly combine several different angles of fighting that it all feels natural, the game tends to spawn enemies behind you, to the side of you, maybe in the background, and all of them equally a threat. You can of course destroy all of them, with just four simple tools.
Astebreed has 5 weapons to the players disposal, each can be used in various ways to destroy the attacking Filunes.
First off is the Scatter shot, which fires bullets in a wide arc infront of the player designed to blanket the screen in a flurry of bullets, effective against largest filunes and tight clusters of fast moving enemies
The second type of bullet is the focus shot, it fires a hail of bullets in a tight straight line directly in front of you, you lose a bit of maneuverability doing this, but the bullets as a whole pack a whole lot more punch. Great for doing some tight focused damage or obliterating a line of enemies travelling in one direction.
The third attack is the Blade Attack, to put it simply you attack with the equipped blade, this cuts through most enemies with ease and also cuts bullets clean in half, find yourself in a tight situation with a hail of bullets incoming, simply cut your way right through them and keep on going. The blade attack also has an innate dash attack which can cut your way through large amounts of enemies in a straight line, but leaves you vulnerable at the end.
The lucis system of your mech can also lockon to enemies in a straight line or 'neutral lockon' by holding the scatter shot or focus shot keys. This allows a hail of 'lucis particles' (not even sure what they're called) to chase enemies (even off screen!) and destroy them for you. You can also use the blade attack instead to do a deadly multi blade dash attack that will attack all locked on enemies on screen.
Its important to note that even though you can cut through enemy bullet patterns, this game is by no means easy, its still just as difficult as this genre is famous for.
The final attack and probably one of the most important is the Ex Attack, which charges relatively quickly and is your 'get out of jail free card' it activates the lucis shield system and makes you completely immune to all attacks for 3-4 seconds.  Great for smashing through seemingly undodgeable patterns.
Enemies will generally fire four types of bullets, Energy balls which can be destroyed by your own mechs scatter or focus shot, yellow bullets which can only be cut, and the dreaded red beam bullets, which can't be cut or shot (these must be avoided at all costs!) Red beam bullets have poor tracking and homing. Movement is key. They're a few other types of shots, but most others are unique to certain types of enemies.
Astebreed features a tutorial and 3 levels of difficulty with varying enemy patterns in each one, so you'll be able to have fun with each difficulty you attempt, knowing you'll get a different game each time!
The game is relatively short and can be beaten in a single sitting (50minutes to 1hr) but features extremely high replayability in the form of difficult achievements and online leaderboards to aim for.
Overall this game I highly recommend for those wanting to play a shmup that is both unique, different and challenging.
My only complaint is the story is rather lacklustre (its not really explained very well) and features many bad anime sci-fi tropes. The backgrounds can get REALLY distracting. Theres a scene in chapter 3 where you have to destroy an entire enemy fleet. They're bullets, missiles from the ships, lasers, enemies flying everywhere, Its sometimes way too much to focus on.
I give it a 8/10. Beautiful HD graphics and mechanics show this genre is not running out of ideas and will continue to live on.

This game is a fast-paced, top down, mmo, bullet hell, rogue-like game in which you play as one of 14 classes and work to get better gear and max your stats. This game is extremely fun and rewarding, but also heart-breaking and causes many swear words to be spat out. At the time of writing this, I have a bit over 960 hours on this game. As you can see, it is extremely addicting and will keep you hooked for a long time, even if you quit after your character dies, you'll always come back. It's like a drug actually. As for the actual game it's self it's pretty simple, you run around, shoot at things, dodge bullets from enemies, kill things to obtain better gear and stat potions (which are used to max the 8 stats in the game Attack, Speed, Vitality, Defense, Dexterity, Wisdom, HP, and MP). As stated above, it's extremely fun and rewarding when your character is alive, expecially obatining better gear and loot. As for obtaining said loot, it can drop in a variety of 6 different bags. 1. Brown Bags-low tier gear that can be seen by everyone. 2. Pink Bags-low to mid tier gear that can still be seen by everyone. 3. Purple Bags-a bit higher tier gear than pink bags and can only be seen by you. 4. Blue Bags-Contain stat potions 5. Cyan Bags-Contain high tier gear and can only be seen by you 6. White Bags- Contain untiered items and can only be seen by you. (Untiered=better than any tiered items)
Anyway, there is a lot more to this game but I don't feel like explaining everything that in-depth so I'll just go over my few gripes with the game.
1. THE COMMUNITY - Oh boy, in a game about working together to beat dungeons and to help each other, you would think the community would be nice to each other but nope. There are people who drag enimies on to AFK players, leechers who just sit in the starting room and teleport once the people have made it to the boss, just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in general who get angry whenever they don't get the loot that they want and when you get it they rage at you, scammers, and sooo much more. I've found myself kind of playing solo at most times simply because I don't want to deal with the horrid community in this game.
2. KABAM (Sometimes) - Everyone always complains about Kabam because they made the game easier by adding pets and by making Tops (top tier gear) able to be bought in the Nexus. Although that was annoying, they've gotten better. Such as Wis-mod making 3 classes (Paladin, Preist, and Mystic) have their wisdom affect how much damage and how long their ability should last. Also, they added some dungeons (shatters, Shaitans, the Epic dungeons, Belladona's garden, etc.) they also brought back a couple old dungeons (LoD and BeachZone).
All in all, the game has a couple problems, but most games do. This game is very challenging and I love it very much.
Update: With the Deca Games takeover, it hasn't been very long but I can already tell this game is going to improve tenfold. The new owners seemingly actually care about the game, rather than the former owners just kinda sweeping it under the rug for months. Many people who quit the game because of Kabam are coming back and the community finally feels a little less toxic.

For me this game is a great fusion between TBS gameplay and character customization. It lets me make unique soldiers I enjoy and end up caring about... then subjects them to serious tactical challenges as I figure out how to stay ahead of the 8-ball and keep them alive and advancing. Where the game lacks there is a strong modding base to draw from, so between modding and randomly generated game elements, there always seems like more cause for replays. I have plenty more characters to recruit for Legend playthroughs...
People have different experiences with game stability. I have had very little instability other than through sloppy modding, so I can attest to game problems not being a certainty. The issues I've had with the game itself have at worst required me to go to the main menu and reload... like once every 100hrs. Other issues are not game-breaking and just sorta part of the environment you're immersed in.
The game is definitely different than XCOM 2012, improved in many ways- graphics, gameplay, pacing of the narrative development, challenge, creature models, customization- and lacking in only one: the horror-genre dread of engagement (because it's a lot more action-oriented now). XCOM 2 is a faster-paced version with less insanity dealing with the "global expansion" aspect, but both have a steep learning curve and carelessness is met with the usual mercilessness by the AI.
I'll recommend the game because the devs did a great job investing in the core aspects of their franchise, but it's obviously a bit of a niche genre that it fits into. Still it's worth giving a shot if you enjoy a more sophisticated process of liberating the world from alien occupation. 300+hrs so far have more than given me my money's worth...

As a shoot-em-up game, Astebreed's very forgiving for first timers, giving high leeway with shielding and little-to-no contact-damage. That said, Astebreed won't forgive you if you let your guard down, especially within the last half of the game (and without remorse on Hard).
One of the most notable things about this game is how many enemies there are-- not so much in number of styles, but in sheer quantities. The number of cannon fodder enemies that appear starts out already high, and steadily rises as you progress. It might seem like a swarm of (at least early on) docile, non-colliding foes could be a breeze to handle, but when you need to aim or lock-on enough at the extremely hostile foes hiding amidst the clouds of mooks-- or especially if you choose to aim for a High Score and can't seem to keep up with their endless numbers-- you will find them just as much of a risk as the targets firing all their rockets from behind it all.
I will be frank, this game is not for everyone. It's usual price combined with the duration of the storymode may rub some the wrong way. It best with a controller, and the story can be hard to follow--not for lack of cohesive plot, but for it's all Japanese audio leaving the translated text as the only means to follow along (and it's none too easy to read with 100 other things to focus on). Additionally, though I'm none too sure if it wasn't just a lag-based fluke, in one or two rare moments some of the dialogue text had issues with it's timing, transitioning too soon or slowly, or skipping a line entirely (though it is forgivable in that you can piece together whats missed via intuiton).
That said, for those who do enjoy quick and frantic gameplay with a fair number of options in combating unending enemy hordes, who like beautifully rendered CG environments and some fairly enjoyable and fitting background musics, or just love SHMUPS in general, then this would be a must-have for the collection.

Slightly biased towards the devs of this game, but only because I've watched them polish this game for quite a while. What it started from, the assets they hand crafted themselves (didn't borrow or steal), the fact they got a great musician that actually fit their game to work with the sound track and so forth sell me a game. I think of it as investing in someone's idea and dream as much as buying a product. They always chatted me up and answered my questions, so I  pre-ordered this long before Steam was even a reality. I'd probably give them a positive review even if the game were a steaming heap.... which it's NOT.
While this game can be a frantic iso-mecha-tric shooter, the controls are very much akin to tanks and mecha. Which means A and D will swivel the torso, W and S and will move front to back,  while mouse actually moves the aim. This takes quite a bit of getting used to, but tip is to look at the spotlights that the vehicle shines on the ground. One will be for the body/movement and one will be for aiming. The problem as it stands now is they can be harder to distinguish, become blocked by terrain/obsticles and generally get disorienting. I wouldn't have the game control any other way, however. It's true to the idea behind the vehicles and its something a bit fresher feeling over the generic point/click/move. There is a skill curve that makes sense and it's not just throwing square wheels on a car to make it harder to drive. This game will be something you will get better at playing as you play it. If you want a game you can sit down and be great at and win immediatly, then consider something else.
Tip: I'd recommend starting with the tank as the graphic serves a much better indication as to how to control it.
The control set actually lends itself to a slightly slower gameplay that requries a bit of tactical movement on the players behalf. This isn't a game where you will endlessly kill mindless enemies. Your ammo is quite limited, though can sometimes be refilled by random towers or rare drops. Position matters where you shoot the enemy. Charging things without considering that you are just wasting ammo by shooting them from the front is bad form. You do more damage from the side or the back, so dodging and timing shots can be much more benefical over going pure John Rambo. There are also "Special" weapons. Smoke bombs which obstruct enemy view so it can help escape and positioning. Camo for the sneaky type and EMP grenades that I just rarely use.
Tip: To save ammo, use your melee attack on smaller enemies like footmen and in desperation against light craft. Stealth can combine with this for fun results.
Isometric was just a perfect choice. It's very reminiscent of the 16/32 bit era of "Strike" games which pleases me greatly. Everything can be destroyed and you can carve a path through the level with your machine. Each weapon can affect the enviroment differently and of course there's explosive structures that can be used tactically.
Tip: Blow everything up. It's cathartic.
As a huge fan of synthwave/cyberpunk music, I was already a fan of Makeup and Vanity Set. His soundtrack for this game just helps a great deal setting the atmosphere. It's always nice to see a game seek someone that works better than just getting someone to fill in because their cousin can make beats. The soundtrack is very much part of the game. It's not just an afterthought asset at the bottom of the budget. Devs take note!
As far as content, there is much much more to be added. I'll update this review accordingly to reflect this. Right now you can do basic runs and it's generally a sandbox with everything unlocked. You have complete mission freedom. You can kill a set number of enemies, find the commanders and kill them all or take out a few of the orbital cannons and advance to the next. In the future there will be unlocks and money as well as many more missions and tilesets. Also coming will be controller support, which may be a better alternative for the controls for some.
A very thought-out design from top to bottom. The dev/brother team knew what they wanted to make and executed in a masterclass fashion. They have built an amazingly solid housing for their game. Now, the rest is just moving some more content into it and making the price tag more tempting.  The price doesn't bother me in the least. In a world of cheap sales, that only bring disposable titles or F2P games that are more timetraps than video games, I'd always pay premium for something like this. 20$ is hardly "premium" pricing though. I would have paid half that for the soundtrack alone.  This is a game I can revisit because after all it's actually a video game. Not storybook on rails or a grindfest because grinding because modern video games. Also: MECHA!!.. extremely underused theme.

I have to say Okami is one of my all time favorite games. I played it on a friend's system and really loved it. I was happy to be able to buy my own copy, and on a system I owned. The game itself is good and I like the art style.
My main problems come down to the little things. It doesn't feel like a good port of the game. It kind of feels like they did the bare minimum to  get it to work on the computer and update the graphics so it doesn't pixilate. You can't change the graphic size in game, only it's "quality".
There is no controller customization, although I have to say the built in steam controller settings are fantastic. There is no real mouse support in menus. Yes it controls the brush and camera but no cursor no clicking on things. The choice on keyboard controls are just odd. They use WASD for movement then put all of the menu control and such on Backspace and the enter below it. No way to change that or even the option to use like the # pad.
All in all I'm sad to say it looks like they saw a chance to take a popular older game and squeeze it for money without actually doing any work to make it behave like a computer game. They did the minimal amount of work so that it could run on a computer.

Don't let my lack of hours played fool you. I've beaten this game in its entirety once before.
Okami is one of the best video games I’ve ever played and this is why.
About so many years ago, the first time I ever played it. I didn’t realize going in what kind of game it really was. It wasn’t explained properly to me, I blame this on poor marketing at the time and on myself for not doing more research before buying it.
So I start this game up, and the first thing you’ll notice is this very long and drawn out opening cut scene, not much to it mind you but it tells a simple story well, sets a stage and the moment it closes, it opens with someone ending the world, or well you know, getting the end started as if he never really heard the story we just heard, himself.
Open to and without giving too much away, we meet our main characters. This game is fun, it’s dire and it’s right to the point. From the very beginning you realize exactly who you are and how you as a character fit into this story being told. I was hooked. I laughed out loud many, many times. It’s use of humor is downright disarming at times.  So many times we watch what could be a good movie ruin it’s own jokes because the film maker didn’t trust their audience to “get it” and they didn’t understand to wait a few beats before moving on to the next joke. Not a problem here. The humor never serves to undercut how serious the game is and it doesn’t come at the expense of the player’s disbelief, most importantly. Hard line to walk for some. This being said, I laughed out loud many times during this game.
But why might you love it as I do?
Have you have ever played a game and wished with every fiber of your being at the end, it wasn’t actually going to stop? That was my reaction the very first time I played Okami. I was getting to the end, I beat the final boss… and that’s when you find out you’re maybe half way done. It was a revelation, I had never played a game that set me up so well that I didn’t even understand the primary conflict wasn’t in fact close to over. This game does such a great job of defying your expectations giving way to genuinely welcome surprises.
I’d go on but I really don’t want to ruin this game for you. It’s a steal at 20 bucks. The art style alone made sure this game is ageless. Add on top of that, the fact that it will most likely be on sale during the Winter Sale starting on the 21st on this month… just throwing that out there and I still didn’t wait because well it’s amazing and as I said a steal even at 20 bucks. Heat Signature is a fun game for I'd say the first 5-10 hours. It gets very repetitive towards the endgame and only becomes fun for your average completionist, and even if you are the completionist, the achievements are quite easy.
Story and Lore:
There are 4 Factions. Offworld, The Foundry, The Sovereign, and the Glitchers. Your goal is to liberate the different nodes in each of the faction's territory, ultimately liberating the stronghold of the faction. Liberating nodes is quite simple, really, do missions, gain enough progress to liberate the next node. Other than that as the main hook of the story, there isn't anything much else. Characters come with personal missions, steal this, rescue him, kill her, and that's really the only thing about the characters that is unique, aside from the randomized starter gear. You can find a few NPCs to talk to after liberating a stronghold that provide a background on the inner workings of the Faction, but not that much.
5/10 Story.
Gameplay:
Hotline Miami, but with slow motion, and in space. You get a mission from the missions board varying in difficulty, and will pay more the harder it is so that you can purchase more gear for your character. Then, you get in your pod, fly to the ship, and lock on.
Once you're inside, you have to complete your mission. You can pause time and make whatever preparations you need to while paused. While learning it, it's very interesting, as the feeling of killing many enemies at once in one room using only a few wrenches is nice, but after playing the game for a bit, it again gets very repetitive. Pause, hit, move on.
There are various things to help you do your missions, teleporters that only work if there's an unblocked path from your character to your destination, teleporters that swap you with another person, and teleporters that bring you to your destination temporarily. There are things that make you invisible, make you 5x faster than everything else, give you a shield. There are only 3 types of guns, with a few characteristics making them unique. Basically, there's not a lot of gear yet in the game.
7/10 Gameplay.
Summary:
Sorry, I suck at writing reviews.
But as I said in the start, it's fun for a while, but get's very repetitive, not much else to do aside from the same old missions on the same 4 faction ships varying in size. I would only recommend getting this if you aren't limited to a small budget, like me. It's a nice quick fun experience but I have a very limited budget for steam, so if you have like, 5 bucks or something, save it up instead of getting this.
Overall: 6.7/10

For those interested, I'll throw information about what this game is about, and its' relevance to previous titles.
1) First of all, it does not include at all Rogue's character Shae Comarc. One might think that since Rogue's ending sets foot for AC Unity, the story might continue in an interesting way. But this does not happen.
2) Modern day story still continues from Rogue's, but its minimal. You are always stuck in the animus, and only see Rebecca once, and then just hear her voice throughout the game.
3) Like many people have complained, the combat system has changed. You do not use your hidden blades anymore in battles. You can only use them in stealth kills, either from behind, or jumping from rooftops or towers or what not. In battles you only combat with swords, or any other heavy weapon available to you. And guns of course.
4) Parkour system is a little irritating at points, but not terrible. One major thing they've taken out, or at least what I experienced, was the ability to jump from corner to another one. When climbing a high wall for example, and moving the camera to be able to jump to what is behind you. That is out as far as I've seen in the game.
There are more flaws in the story that I encountered, but I don't want to spoil that. Just play the game and see for yourself.
Despite all said previously, I did like the game in its' own way. I have read many hating reviews and comments and opinions about the game, so I wanted to try it for myself. And I did like it, the story is fun, and the french revolution was a lot of fun to play in an AC title. I was just disappointed that it does not even mention Shae Cormac at all. I believe that the somewhat lower reviews for this game, comparing with the previous one, are just fair. This is simply not as good as the previous XCOM. It has a lot of performance issues, incredible long loading times even on SSD, and that 720p resolution looks simply awful - don't buy unless you can play in Full HD. There were some gameplay changes that made no sense: why to remove the pistols (except for snipers) ?, while others were well done: overwatching shots are not all spend on the first target that moves, like in the first game. Same thing for history. It wasn't as interesting for me as the one from the first game, but yet, they deserve credit for introducing variety and not making an entire equal game. Now the aliens control Earth, and our base is a airship that moves around the planet, which obviously also affects gameplay and gives a refreshed strategy experience.
Another big difference is the difficult level. The previous XCOM was difficult, but this one is even worse. I played the previous one in Ironmode, but this one I had to use a lot of save and load "cheat" just not to get crushed, and I'm not sure if I even want to try Ironmode. However, the special missions are easier on this one (didn't need to load and save on neither and no soldiers lost - not even close). The base defense one was a piece of cake (while on the previously one was VERY difficult), and the final mission was not very challenging. Normal missions were way more difficult.
Oh, btw, timed missions suck.
But overall, it's still a very good game, because it's still the XCOM formula, with great mechanics and great gameplay.

This game is so, so good.
The gameplay, if you can call it that, consists of two parts: breaking into systems and exploring them. Breaking in is intense. You'll find yourself panicking as you type out commands as fast as you can in order to beat the trace, and when you just barely make it, you'll sigh in relief and wipe sweat off the palms of your hands. Even though it's just text and a little GUI (graphic user interface), it reels you in like nothing else.
The exploring is actually my favourite part of the game, because the game rewards your curiosity with humour, story, and extra servers and .exe's. A large portion of this game can easily be missed if you're not looking, so LOOK EVERYWHERE. If you see an IP address, it'll lead to something. Most servers have chat logs, which don't serve any gameplay purpose, but are usually hilarious. Some of the servers can even be reached before the story gives them to you, which doesn't spoil the story so much as give you this satisfaction from going where you're not supposed to go.
And that's the real magic of Hacknet: it makes you think like a hacker. There's no real hand-holding, so it's up to you to figure out what to do. You have a set of tools and a bunch of servers to mess with, and from there, you just do whatever you want. Try to go where it seems you're not supposed to, because that's exactly what hacking is. The game gets out of your way and lets you hack, which is why it doesn't feel like a game at all.
Pros:
+ Breaking into stuff is intense and rewarding
+ Exploring is fun and rewarding
+ Simple enough to be accessible to scrubs like me
+ Complex enough to make you feel like a badass hacker
+ Soundtrack is good enough that I don't feel a need to turn the volume down
Cons:
- To get the most out of the game, you need basic familiarity with a command-line interface
P.S. Play through the game in one stretch. Don't put it down for very long or you'll forget where everything is.

This is a great game, with top-notch production quality.  The developers clearly put in a ton of effort to create a well-polished game accessible to as wide an audience as possible.
The first thing to note is that this game is far more forgiving than your typical bullet hell shmup, which is great for people like me who tend to be terrible at that genre.  While many shmups involve a tiny hitbox and a ton of finesse in movement alone, Astebreed gives you a shield which recharges after not being hit for a few seconds.  This might be a turn-off to hardcore fans of the genre, but I would argue that Astebreed still manages to keep things interesting in its own ways, while also being more accessible to a wider audience.
Astebreed features dynamic gameplay switching between top-down, horizontal, and behind-your-mech perspectives throughout the game.  In terms of attacks, you have two types of normal shots (spread and focused), which each have a unique charge/lock-on mechanism, and you have a sword with close-range and dash attacks.
The game is equipped with an introduction section and a set of tutorials to get you fully up-to-speed on the various mechanics, including how scoring works.
In terms of playthrough length, you're looking at around an hour (and that's if you don't skip cutscenes), but that's not terribly unusual for the genre.  In terms of replayability, the game has multiple difficulty settings and mechs, and naturally there are leaderboards for each stage and total score.

The dystopian narrative also works well with the mechanics and ties in tightly with the 'who do you trust?' and 'unreliable narrator' themes common to hacking mythos.

The standard attacks include a concentrated stream of bullets and a spread shot, each of which can be charged up to deliver a homing attack that will help Eleminate enemies for a limited time, and give you some   manuvering room.  Dujinsoft studio Edelweiss accomplishes just about everything it sets out out to do with Astebreed. It's inventive, beautiful, and absorbing. The music is catchy and perfectly fitting. Darkest Dungeon is a dark roguelike RPG with heavy empasis on the mental state of the heroes you hire. The game places you as the new owner of the family manor and surrounding grounds after your ancestor met his untimely demise by his own hand (after screwing literally everything up and placing you in charge to clean it up). The game opens to a prompt pretty much telling the player they will fail, and fail you will. RNG is a huge factor in the game, attacks hitting or missing, DoTs being applied, dodging, suprise chance, CRITS, damage gap on weapons, etc. Many complain how nothing matters because everything is random and how heroes die in one turn without them being able to do anything about it. However many of these aspects can be influenced in your favor using trinkets general buffing which can increase accuracy, increase DoT application chance, stop suprise attacks with scouting and have a high light level, buffing damage, etc. Such an occurance of what some reviews describe can be possible but would require the stars to align on a specifc day of taco pizza. To sum it up, dont let reviews that compain about RNG disway your opinion of the game because it feels oh so good when your able to pull through a dungeon that was kicking you butt.

Astebreed is a sort of shoot'em'up / 3D mecha game hybrid. There's a fairly complicated melee system which makes the game very different from normal shooters. In addition to a generic shot and melee you have the ability to lock-on to enemies in an area.
The view of the gameplay shifts throughout the game; scrolling directions change and sometimes you only shoot enemies in the background. This is the best implementation of this I've seen so far, I felt it didn't disturb my gameplay at all unlike say in  Eschatos or Ether Vapor.
A single playthrough while skipping all cutscenes takes about 30 minutes, which is average for a shmup. There is also chapter select to play each of the 6 chapters.
Pros:
+ Extremely impressive presentation for an indie game. Graphics, music and sound effects are all top notch
+ Shooting and melee combat systems are merged nicely. There is a lot of depth to how the systems can be used.
+ Approachable to beginners of the genre due to varied difficulty options, lifebar and a comprehensive tutorial
+ Simple intuitive scoring system; shoot things with your shot or lock-on to increase a multiplier, then get a lot of points by killing enemies using melee attacks with a high multiplier
+ Well produced (but generic) anime storyline to follow throughout the game. I'm assuming the japanese voice actors are pretty good as well.
+ Lots of extras and achievements to unlock
Cons:
- It can be very difficult to see bullets and your hitbox when there's a lot of stuff going on
- Some unskippable cutscenes even with story dialogue turned off in options
- No 'super difficult' mode for hardcore fans of the genre. There's also not that much actual bullet dodging on hard mode because about half of all bullet patterns can be cancelled with melee strikes.
- Lack of cohesion in enemy behavior: the same enemy type might shoot completely different attack patterns in different waves. Some attacks aren't telegraphed well (very fast red lasers without warning, etc)

It’s similar to games like Impossible Mission, Max Headroom, and Project Firestart - yet unlike any of them. Feeling like it fell out of time somewhere and got ported to the PC in the process. I recognized immediately the itch the game would scratch, the nuanced design and throwback to that era is readily apparent. And at the end credits, I wasn’t disappointed. If anything, I wished it had been more obscure and obtuse to play.
To be clear, there is not much in terms or story or action here. It’s an experience and a trip to the past for those who still recognize the road it takes.

This is a really fun, frenetic isometric action game. The controls are tight and responsive, although they may take a bit of getting used to. Enemies are diverse in both attributes and behavior, and the environments are dense and interesting. I really respect the devs for choosing to not color every explosive element red, although I cursed their names the first time i discovered this fact.
The graphics are excellent. I don't know what voodoo magic allows such accurate-looking lighting effects in a 2d game, but it is strong, and arcane. You really have to see it in motion to appreciate it. The overall visual density is high, and honestly pretty busy, but it gets much easier to read the action after a few games.
The game presents a stiff challenge, but not an unfair one. At first you'll find yourself overwhelmed by all the threats coming at you from every direction, but soon you'll learn how to use the environment to your advantage and manage the flow of battle. Smoke is your friend!
There are six vehicles to choose from in the current build (there have been more in pre-release builds and certainly will be again) and many different weapons, each with their own strengths and weaknesses. This level of choice is one of the game's greatest strengths, but may also be the biggest stumbling block for new players, since it's easy to choose a loadout that doesn't have good synergy, and get completely owned.
Pro tip: try the loyalist mech "Touro" with the cannon "Abbot", machine gun "Mae Dois", and smoke launcher. It's a very powerful combo. But definitely don't stick to it! Try all kinds of things and have a great old time.
I strongly recommend this game to anyone who likes arcade or action games, as well as anyone who thinks trucks, tanks, and mechs are cool.

I bought it the day of the release. I was used to Terraria and I was excited to see the result in Sci-Fi (it was promoted as a spiritual successor of Terraria).
My Avian explorer was born few hours later (you can choose 7 different races each with its own backgrounds, styles, weapons, armors and space ships).
Together we built huge bases, traveled in space to discover worlds, fought tons of creatures and vanquished dangerous bosses.
Farmed to cook new recipes or search for materials and upgrade our racial armor.
There were so much things to do i was already addicted!
I even fought an army of space penguins lead by a small one in a huge flying saucer !!!!
But after 25 hours, my character died. He was wiped with an update.
My little Avian came back; ready to venture further in this huge universe.
20 hours of fun. But spoiled with and other character wipe...
And you know what?
I didn't complain about it. Contrary to some people who forced Chuckle Fish to use a test version for its updates: something that many forgot to notice in their rants in comments about this year without an update on the released version.
This game was made with so much passion that I couldn't blame the team behind it.
The reason why we have been patient, why we are so many to support it...
It's because Starbound is why we still put one's heart and soul into its video game.
Starbound is the greatness of video games. Beautiful, vast, cute, clever and for all audiences that will surely catch your heart! So yes this game is about heart, even music are so beautiful that it might makes you feel as nostalgic as in Elder Scrolls franchise (still need more tracks on Starbound but it’s a really, REALLY good start).
And one year after its release they've dropped a HUGE update and now we can really enjoy the work they’ve done during all this time.
To sum up:
New quest system focused around an outpost you can access via galactic portals where you can find traders and npc to start new quests (first ones serves as tutorials). Tons of new characters, monsters and bosses.
Reworked worlds generation, every planets has a place of interest.
Crafting is deeper but tools ,more efficient, loose their durability quicker. Tons of new items, weapons, armors, clothes, materials and blocks.  Farming is easier, you can find more plants on planets !
Your ship can be repaired and upgraded to gain new rooms and tons of other cool options. Space travel has been reworked, easier to use but with harder requirements, in each system type has an upgrade necessary for your ship. In general you have to defeat a boss and find materials in the deepest levels of planets and  you now need a special fuel to travel in other solar systems (coal in FTL drive ? It's over !).
Combat has changed, ranged attacks uses stamina and close combat weapons can aim in a larger radius.
You can catch creatures and even tame them to help you in combat. And of course... VEHICLES ! They gave us tons of new vehicles ! Each race has its own but you can craft many others. From the sci-fi walker to the car or even boats.
But i will stop here my list beacause there is too much to write...
So if you read this review:
Don't go anywhere else on the store. Don't even hesitate.  Because this game is NOW a must buy!
(Especially to thank this marvelous update and to have more than 100 hours of fun for this price.
But beware, there are still some small bugs. Use open gl launch to play the game and wait a bit. The loading is long. Few more updates and the game will be a classic).

When I was first presented with the opportunity to cover Brigador, I’ll admit, I had no clue what it was. I did a little bit of research and discovered the upcoming game, being developed a group of four guys under the name ‘Stellar Jockeys‘, striven to be a isometric hybrid of ‘Syndicate‘ and ‘Mechwarrior‘. After reading that I was determined to jump into Brigador without any further knowledge of the game and see how much fun I had, and let me tell you; I had a ton of fun.
Damn is Brigador a beautiful game. The game is set in the bright and bustling isometric cityscape of Solo Nobre. At launch there are nine very detailed levels/districts to Solo Nobre, each with their own unique but similar layout. At the beginning of each mission (dubbed contract’s in the game), you choose from one of three categories: tanks, mechs, and anti-gravity vehicles. The tanks are typically defensive, the mechs primarily offensive, and the anti-gravity vehicles are fast. Each mech has it’s own weapons and play style as well as toughness when taking damage.
From here you’re thrown into the contract you selected and begin dishing out massive destruction to anything and everything in the district. The entire map is fully destructible, including attacking enemy vehicles, all of the buildings and enemy defenses, and even the civilians attempting to flee the city from your carnage. There are quite a few unique weapons in Brigador, all of which take some getting used to. You move using the W-A-S-D and a mouse, but it’s not as simple as it sounds. The movement is similar to Resident Evil in that you use the A and D keys to rotate your vehicle in places, W to move forward, and S to move backwards. You have a red and a blue line that project from your vehicle in different arcs and help show you where your weapons will be fired. Using this system you can aim high, low, and even around buildings to take out aerial or ground enemies at command.
Brigador is tough. On top of the intricate(but fair)movement system, the enemies themselves are quite challenging. By design, there is no saving or restarting, so you must play through the district’s clearing out enemies and completing the objectives of your contract to move forward. While keeping track of your ammunition is certainly important, there are ammo stations scattered across each map, and defeating some enemies will result in them dropping ammo packs to replenish your ammo. That being said, successfully completing a level carries over your current ammunition counts and health, meaning to ‘beat’ the game you would have to complete each district in one sitting and straight playthrough.
If you’re a fan of isometric ‘top down’ shooter type games, Brigador is definitely for you. As I mentioned before, it’s an extremely beautiful game, and a ton of fun. Destroying the city of Solo Nobre while wiping out your enemies and completing your contracts does require a bit of strategic shooting, but is enjoyable the whole way. While the game itself was a bit too difficult for me to successfully clear all districts in one sitting, I feel as though that’s necessary with a game like Brigador. The only thing I’d ask for is perhaps more of a story or campaign rather than just “Complete Objectives in all Districts’, but after playing through all of them there is definitely the feeling of some repetition.
Brigador enters early access on October 20th at the price of $20 on Steam and Humble and plans to add more content throughout the early access stage.
This review score is based on its Early Access launch. We may or may not do another review for this game once it enters the full retail launch phase.

The soundtrack is good. The visuals are good. The mechanics are good. The map design is good.
Brigador's a good mech game, which seems to be a rare commodity these days. It's an isometric shooter with systems bigger and more complex than 'put your mouse on the bad guy robot and press the button,' the biggest of which is the aiming system, since it's three-dimensional. You can overshoot or fall short of targets, and the camera works in conjunction with this. Unlike another recent top-down shooter with a banging synth soundtrack, the shifting camera won't give you motion sickness, and you won't get oneshot from offscreen. Differing armor values for front, sides, and rear (for enemies AND for players) means that flanking isn't just viable, it's vital, and different acceleration, handling, and speed while traveling in different directions in different vehicles means that even two vehicles of the same class feel and play differently.
Your tower tank can plow through enemy and environment alike while absorbing blow after blow; your mech can peek and retreat around corners, fire over low walls or crouch to hide behind them, and stomp anything that dares get close; your main battle tank is fast and maneuverable with a low profile and a speed boost for hit-and-run attacks; and your antigrav can weave in and out of buildings, strafe targets without exposing vulnerable side armor, or belly flop on enemies who make the mistake of letting you get close.
I've been playtesting the game since early alpha builds and the progress it's made is astounding. The game is gorgeous and never stops being fun to play. 60 hours later I still constantly get the itch to boot it up and throw together a new build to see how far I can get with it. There's really no game on the market that plays quite like it. This game is good and you should buy it.

This game coming out to PC is a dream come true to me.
I've tried and failed to ever get Wii or PS2 emulators to run this game stable on PC. Finally.. a dream come true.
It's not a perfect port, but rarely are ports from consoles ever perfect. However, it's stable. It runs flawlessly smooth at high settings with an i5-3470 and 760GTX.
Some of the rough points with the port quality is that the game eats up CPU more than GPU. My GPU fan never throttled up the entire time playing, but the game is a port from the PS3, so it should run fine off modern integrated graphics without need for a dedicated card at all. I'll have to see how well I can get it to run on my tablet that plays Skyrim beautifully smoothly. Another was having to tell Steam to enable controller support, but I believe that is a Steam issue more than game issue.
People complain about the 30FPS, but I can't tell a difference from it on PC and having played it on PS2, Wii, and PS3 before, it plays identically as well, it's just the PS3 HD version ported to PC, as far as I can tell, nothing added, nothing removed, game is rather untouched except for steam achievements. But the winner to me about it is that the game is stable and an amazing game to have brought to modern systems/hardware that I can continue to enjoy for many more years to come.
With all the hours I have put into this game so far, it is more stable than a lot of non-ported games I've played before, major titles too. This port is rock solid stable and has never crashed on me, even after hours of gameplay. And you can look at my played hours on Steam.
Thank you to the team that worked on this PC port.

As the first installment in the Hitman series, I will admit that this game shows that the Hitman series had a promising start. However, I would not recommend playing this game unless you're a Hitman fan that's interested in how the series started. I played all the other Hitman games on PS2 and XBox 360, and I was interested to see how it all began with this game, but I finished it feeling a little disappointed.
The Hitman series, as a whole, is action-stealth, usually with a strong emphasis on stealth. I'd say this game is more a strong emphasis on action. Don't get me wrong, there's plenty of stealth to be had, but there are several parts of the game where it's necessary to, say, clear out a room of thugs to continue the objective. I mean, the last mission is nothing but shooting; there's absolutely no stealth option.
The mission locations are basically sandboxes like in the subsequent games, with what seems to be plenty of ways to accomplish the mission on the surface, but oftentimes there's only one surefire way to truly complete your objective; all other "methods" will likely result in blowing your cover and dying. And trust me, you don't want to die in this game; there's no checkpoints or saves, and you have to restart the entire mission if you fail. It's very frustrating to waste 20 minutes and die because you unknowingly trespassed and was shot to death in seconds; it's very easy to die, even with armor on.
The game is buggy; there were times that I pressed escape to open the main menu and it would restart the mission instead, erasing all my progress in that level and forcing me to start from scratch. The game crashed twice in my playthrough, which is to be expected when running such an old game. I got stuck on the world geometry often; there was one time where I had to restart the level right at the end because I was stuck on a flight of stairs.
If you're looking for fun action-stealth gameplay, I would suggest playing the other, later, Hitman games. Codename 47 left a bad impression on me, and I can't see myself playing it for fun anytime soon.

I've spent a long time on this game, had many great moments with my friends on this game, I love this game, or at least I used to.

There were so many people in the game that, because of the crappy game servers that they had cause not many people really played the game, it lagged to the point that most of the time it took at least two attempts to connect to the game server and the game became nearly unplayable. Fortunatly this problem was fixed rather quickly, but that didn't fix the problem that now that more people were playing Trion wanted more of there money. From then on every update made the game more and more bull**** trying to suck the money out of you, so what did me and my friends do? We stopped playing. It had been more of a subconsious thing because they were doing it slowly, little bits at a time, but we were bored about 1 to 1 1/2 years later so we decided to go back back and try it again, it was awful. all the systems were either removed, completely redone, or replaced. The mastery rewards system changed and took away all of the buffs it used to give leaving me a lot weaker than I used to be, they added something to kind of replace the level system once you get to the uber adventure portals call 'power rank' which I found was rigged and  certain classes were a lot weaker than some others when they have the same power rank, nearly everything you could buy in the in-game store using the standard currency 'cubits' now either required the premium currency 'credits', was removed, or was one of the items that required a rediculous amount of cubits that wasn't worth spending on that specific thing. Mixed feelings here - know what you're getting into BEFORE you buy it.
F4 is a GOOD GAME IN GENERAL (sans the current paid mods thing, that was unnecessary) but as a FALLOUT game it is TERRIBLE.
Pros
-Combat in general has been totally overhauled to match up with modern FPS standards, and the fights are pretty intense with scaled enemies.
-A decent pool of weapons with varying levels of customization. Pipe weapons, while rather weak, are SUPER MODDABLE. Start with a pistol and turn it into an SMG; get a pipe revolver and turn it into a hard-hitting sniper rifle - theres a lot of room to wiggle there, and thats just objectively awesome.
-All enemies are dangerous and unique. In previous 3D titles the enemies had rather generic actions, and some were no threat to you even naked - but in 4 there are enemies that burrow, legitimately fly (they previously hovered a certain distance from the ground) have cinematic attacks and executions and even suicide bomb you!
- High moddability, even without importing models, animations and scripting. There are plenty of tutorials to get you started as well
Cons
-Lacks many of the RPG elements of choice that made the series what it is
-performance issues. with bethesda you come to expect that. Its nice when stuff gets fixed, but until then, SOMEONE knows a workaround
-Fairly shallow story. This is a big one, as the story was the defining factor for the Fallout series. A predefined history, linear questlines, no karma mechanic and very few, annoyigly limited opportunities to really influence the world beyond building a settlement have really impacted the scope of the game.
###
For an accurate comparison: In New Vegas, completing the game without DLC decided the fate of 3 major factions; the NCR, Caesar's Legion and the residents of New Vegas. Your actions could wind up with the genesis of america as it once was; the enslavement of many of the inhabitants of the Mojave; or placing yourself as the kingpin of the Mojave, with an army of robots at your back. the continued existence of a whole chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel depends on you. A large, scattered gang of ex-convicts is poised to become a brand new superpower, and you can either spearhead their operations or eliminate them all. A community of unique super mutants has gathered in hopes of becoming a normal trading town, and to heal themselves of a strange mutation. And this doesnt even include the struggles of the residents of New Vegas itself - this is all going on in the outskirts of the map!
In 4 you rebuild the minutemen (cool, but a rather short process) help the BoS gain a foothold in the Commonwealth and find your son. There are several sidequests and short interactions, but the depth is gone and it hits hard after a while.
The DLC helps with adding more choices, specifically Far Harbor and Nuka World, but it doesnt quite meet the level of their previous titles.
###
All in all, this seems like an attempt to widen their playerbase to the generic fps crowd (i know, i know- it hurts when they try to lump us together. But this is a AAA studio, i think they can learn from their mistakes)
If you want to introduce someone to the Fallout series i recommend starting them here, so they can get used to the world in a more familiar environment before getting the unfiltered, totally raw awesomeness that was 3 and NV.

I really enjoyed this game. The puzzles were fun and challenging and some of the mini-plots were hilarious. While the end missions seemed a little bolted on, it was well worth it.
The only issue I had was understanding how shell overload worked. I was button mashing overload and would eventually get connected, but I didn't figure out the deliberate process. After a few hours I figured it out: when a server is protected with a proxy, each press of the shell overload will increase the speed of a bar that overlays the proxy status text. If you have more shells and press more overloads, that bar goes faster. Once it is full, the proxy is bypassed.
I can imagine that this is not a game for everybody. You are terminal hacking, running programs, erasing logs, and figuring out vectors into target systems. But if you have some Linux experience and you want a hacker-esque game that gives you some thrills and chills, this is well worth it!

I believe that the somewhat lower reviews for this game, comparing with the previous one, are just fair. This is simply not as good as the previous XCOM. It has a lot of performance issues, incredible long loading times even on SSD, and that 720p resolution looks simply awful - don't buy unless you can play in Full HD. There were some gameplay changes that made no sense: why to remove the pistols (except for snipers) ?, while others were well done: overwatching shots are not all spend on the first target that moves, like in the first game. Same thing for history. It wasn't as interesting for me as the one from the first game, but yet, they deserve credit for introducing variety and not making an entire equal game. Now the aliens control Earth, and our base is a airship that moves around the planet, which obviously also affects gameplay and gives a refreshed strategy experience.
Another big difference is the difficult level. The previous XCOM was difficult, but this one is even worse. I played the previous one in Ironmode, but this one I had to use a lot of save and load "cheat" just not to get crushed, and I'm not sure if I even want to try Ironmode. However, the special missions are easier on this one (didn't need to load and save on neither and no soldiers lost - not even close). The base defense one was a piece of cake (while on the previously one was VERY difficult), and the final mission was not very challenging. Normal missions were way more difficult.
Oh, btw, timed missions suck.
But overall, it's still a very good game, because it's still the XCOM formula, with great mechanics and great gameplay.

XCOM 2 adds little to the table from its predecessor and it's plagued by performance issues and random crashes to desktop that make the game unplayable even after months of its release.
PROS:
+ It's still XCOM so expect simple, good, strategic play with meaningful choices and odds at stake.
+ Clear, simple but in-depth game mechanics. Easy to learn, hard to master.
+ Character attachment and customization.
+ Epic Voice Guy.
CONS:
- Play-breaking random crashes to desktop and game freezes even with high-performance computers. It's a toss up.
- It's still XCOM 1 at its core. No new mechanics that improve on the original formula.
- The way the missions are designed force you to a rushed gameplay style 90% of the time.
- More convoluted visuals and transparencies in map make tiling confusing sometimes.
I can't recommend this game in good faith. I want to like it and it's not a bad game but performance and stability issues make it unplayable with no fix on the horizon. I'd wait until it has more months under its belt and devs fix the galloping stability and performance issues. Also go play XCOM 1, it's basically the same with different skins for the enemies, the base and the strategy map, but gameplay wise 99.9% the same.

My little Avian came back; ready to venture further in this huge universe.
20 hours of fun. But spoiled with and other character wipe...
And you know what?

This game was made with so much passion that I couldn't blame the team behind it.
The reason why we have been patient, why we are so many to support it...
It's because Starbound is why we still put one's heart and soul into its video game.
Starbound is the greatness of video games. Beautiful, vast, cute, clever and for all audiences that will surely catch your heart! And one year after its release they've dropped a HUGE update and now we can really enjoy the work they’ve done during all this time.
To sum up:
New quest system focused around an outpost you can access via galactic portals where you can find traders and npc to start new quests (first ones serves as tutorials). Tons of new characters, monsters and bosses.
Reworked worlds generation, every planets has a place of interest.
Crafting is deeper but tools ,more efficient, loose their durability quicker. Tons of new items, weapons, armors, clothes, materials and blocks.  Farming is easier, you can find more plants on planets !
Your ship can be repaired and upgraded to gain new rooms and tons of other cool options. Space travel has been reworked, easier to use but with harder requirements, in each system type has an upgrade necessary for your ship. In general you have to defeat a boss and find materials in the deepest levels of planets and  you now need a special fuel to travel in other solar systems (coal in FTL drive ? It's over !).
Combat has changed, ranged attacks uses stamina and close combat weapons can aim in a larger radius.
You can catch creatures and even tame them to help you in combat. And of course... VEHICLES ! They gave us tons of new vehicles ! Each race has its own but you can craft many others. From the sci-fi walker to the car or even boats.
But i will stop here my list beacause there is too much to write...
So if you read this review:
Don't go anywhere else on the store. Don't even hesitate.  Because this game is NOW a must buy!

Well if there was a so-so vote it would fit this title perfectly. The retro nostalgia fashion is already yesterday's news, and steam is flooded with titles that try hard to hide their swallowness behind low-fi pixel art. Is this the case here? Taken as an adventure proper, with its linearity, absolute lack of challenging puzzles, and shortness, DreamBreak would be passable at best. But as a statement of cold war era's pop culture, or as a clever comment on the awkward and comic aspects of the surrounding political atmosphere, the "game" works surprisingly well. I have no idea whether this was the devs' deliberate intention, or just my interpretation of an otherwise naive dystopian platformer, but for me DreamBreak did the trick to a certain extent. To the game's merits is the visual beauty and the interesting soundtrack.
Having said that, however, the potential for a truly exceptional title was totally missed. There are echoes of "another world" and even of "saboteur" here (anyone out there remembering the zx spectrum's masterpiece??!). But even a zx spectrum espionage puzzle posed greater challenge to mid1980s gamers.
To conclude, if you can approach DreamBreak as a visually attractive comment on our contemporary obsession with a bygone era and its bittersweet reminiscences, go for it. Otherwise, wait for a sale, sit back and enjoy a ride on soviet arcade for an hour or so.
PS for the devs: with such short timeplay please consider making the dlc part of the standard edition. It would be fair for those few, such as myself, who will invest on the title because they want indie devs to keep going😉

This game is simply spectacular.
It's obviously inspired by ZoE, and quite possibly it's the closest thing to ZoE we will get.
This game is a shmup with a twist. You have a wide range of attacks from the get go, including wide and narrow ranged fire and you sword. There is also a dash attack, which is very convinient for changing your positioning and evading. Special attacks is where things get especially interesting. Once the attack is charged it's up to you which special you want to execute. The basic difference is that one is more offensive — dealing a lot of damage to the enemies, and the other is more deffensive — giving you brief invincibility and a chance to evade heavy fire.
You might find that the first few stages are very easy. Don't drop your guard though, try to use the opportunity to learn the mechanics and get yourself comfortable with executing different maneuvers. I can't stress enough how important evading gets later in the game, when suddenly you notice you start getting the Continue Y/N screen a bit too often.
Presentation-wise, the music is good. So far, nothing I would listen to on repeat, but good enough. Visuals are spectacular though. You will want to get destracted from the action by the scenery, because it's that good.
I haven't finished the game yet, but I definitely will. I'm not sure how much replayability the game offers: there are different difficulty settings and you can always try to go for a better score. Regardless, I think I will play through the game at least several times simply because how good the game feels and looks.
Definitely recommend this game to any fan of the genre and anyone who is willing to give it a try.

When I first came across DreamBreak I was really excited by what I saw, the gorgeous pixel art, the lovely soundtrack, which you can listen to in the trailer, and the feeling of a dystopian USSR made me crave for this game.
Now that I finally got my hands on it and beaten it, all I can say is that this is a huge disappointment. I’m all in for this kind of totalitarian dystopian regime setting but despite picturing that scenario, DreamBreak’s world depth is pretty much nonexistent. The real deal breaker for me is the fact that the characters feel very uninspired and have no real personality to them, they feel lifeless and the most you’ll get out of them is a few lines of text.
The only things I can really commend about DreamBreak are the visuals and music. The pixel art style will probably drive a lot of people off but for me it looks pretty great, despite the fact that I’d say that the game has some weird color choices. As far as the music goes, I find it pretty good but it’s essentially very short and on a loop so there’s that. Even then there are times in which the music just suddendly stops which sometimes made me wonder if I had lost audio or something.
For me, one of the major issues with the game is the clunky control scheme and I guess that a lot of people would feel the same way. Even at the end of the game I wasn’t still used to the way the character moved. It’s basically a point & click game but it doesn’t feel like it was made for PC, it feels more like a mobile title and to be honest I can’t really say why, I think it’s something you have to play in order to understand. Another thing that really infuriated me was the lack of a save option, there’s not even an auto-save, because in some areas if you mess up in the slightest bit you’ll be forced to do that zone all over again .
Besides the point & click segments of the game, the game offers some sort of little “mini games” such as plumbing puzzles (like in Bioshock) and the combat itself is also based on a mini game that reminds me of some mobile games. What I mean by that is that if you click in front of you you’ll attack and if you click behind you you’ll enter a defensive stance. I found these funny at the first time but after that it was just more of the same.
I also came across a few bugs like for example, there was this one section in which I had to move a series of crates by using a magnetic crane, but if I grabbed the edge of the crate that was attached to the crane and then moved the crane my character would just sit there grabbing nothing but thin air.

'The kid liked this game. He was sad the adventure came to an end'.  The awesome music, gameplay and visuals. This game is a masterpiece.
Youll be beaten down at every possible turn and still enjoy it. A lot

-There are a total of 6 chapters, with a boss encounter for each. Early stages can be pretty easy, but it can get difficult later on, especially on higher difficulty. It can take you a few attempts during later boss encounters before you figure out their attack pattern and take them down!
-The visuals are fantastic for a SHMUP – everything is crisp and fluid. I really love the excellent art aesthetics and the look for the mechas.
-Also, there are full Japanese voice overs for all of the characters (it's actually pretty good!) Subtitles are available, but you won't be reading much of it during intense fights.
-3 attacks are available to you (4 if you count the EX special which has 3 variants) and each attack has a secondary function. Scatter shots can lock on enemies around you, focus shots lock on enemies in a targeted direction and blade attacks can be used to dash across the screen. Destroying enemy shots with the blade will charge the EX meter faster.
-You’ll become real familiar with your arsenal – you won’t just spam one attack, especially if you’re a score chaser. You'll use blade attacks to rack up points, switch between shots depending on your position, cancel enemy projectiles with your blade, line up foes and dash across the screen with the blade dash to destroy enemies or avoid danger, and find the perfect moment to unleash your EX special to annihilate your foes.
-You can take some punishment before you die. Your "health" is your shields which recharges over time to a certain degree.
-The camera perspective will change during combat keeping each encounter fresh. It switches between side-scrolling, top-down, and 3D perspectives.
-Astebreed definitely has replayability. Hard mode is extremely challenging. You also have the option to turn on scoring to test your skills and compete against other players’ scores on the online leaderboards.
-There are unlockables! Hard mode, art, model viewer, and the ability to start with a different mecha becomes available after beating the game.

After reading some recent reviews, I feel like it's necessary to stand out and defend for my favorite game.
All I'm saying now is the truth.
First of all, after the phase 2 update the tutorial for new players is "optimized" compared to the old one , and it does tell you the basic mechanic of the game. But after the tutorial and few mandatory PVE games you have to save 11k for enforcer, which is an expert level CQB(close quarter battle) ship. I see players firing enforcer's weapon to their enemies 10k+ units away everyday. Pioneer, venturer and sentinel are good starter ships, we need them back.
Second, as you level up you will unlock the crew system and implants, you get crew member from drops pods which can be obtained up to 4 everyday( login reward+6games) and you need DNA which can be obtained from drop pods as well to fill the "template" if the crew. You can buy these things from store of course, but new players defenitely can use 1 million credits on better place(new ships).   The implant system, has its own rule and it's actually a small buff to the ship whiteout breaking the game. For those who complain about implants here is my reason:
Every crew member cannot have 2 same implants, so the "put 10 damage reduction implants on crew and make the ship unkillable" is nonsense. Every implant only gives a small amount of bug to the ship, like 0.8% attack damage, -2% jump prep, 2% repair effeciency.  It's really not a big deal because the team combination is mor important. 2 "unkillable" colossus or gladiator with 2 CQB ships will still be bashed by sniper and mobility comb.
Third, the ship balance, in current gameplay there are several ships being overpowered( e.g. Displacer paladin) ECG(the developer) already did several adjustments in the past months, and there will be more in the future. As I climb up to 1900mmr these ships are overwhelmingly powerful in the right hands, and some ships are inferior comparing to them( enforcer , presecutor comparing to brawler) . BUT, there are so few people that can really dominate game and new players below 1k mmr hardly have a chance to meet them, why don't you spend time on getting used to this game and play the ships you are good at while waiting for the next balance update?
Finally I want to express some personal opinions: this is a good game, but small player base makes it hard to provide a good experience like you get from other moba games. It is free2play, it worth trying, if you like it, give it a good review, if you don't like it, write reason upon truth.
